description: US-33 Pick the Art des Nachweises instead of typing it. FOUR SCREENS ask what kind of proof of need a household brought — registration (/kunden/neu), the renewal on a customer record (/kunden/[id]), the renewal at the counter (/ausgabe) and the waiting-list applicant form (/warteliste) plus its promotion form — and all of them ask it as an EMPTY TEXT BOX. The same half a dozen answers are retyped week after week by four different people from memory. The typing is tedious; THE VARIANTS ARE WORSE — „Jobcenter-Bescheid", „Jobcenter Bescheid", „JC-Bescheid" and „jobcenter" are one kind of notice recorded four ways and nothing in the software can tell that they are. THE FIX is a small vocabulary DF maintain themselves: a list of Nachweis-Arten on /einstellungen and a native drop-down wherever the type is asked for. NOT A CLOSED LIST — a staff member at the counter with a notice nobody has seen before must not abandon a half-filled form to go and configure one, so the drop-down carries the configured types AND A „Sonstiges" OPTION that opens a free-text field. What they type there is stored as the certificate's type and DOES NOT silently join the list. THE LIST IS NOT A POLICY VERSION: SettingsVersion is append-only for one reason — a hand-out recorded last March must still be priceable with the rule that applied then (ADR-005) — and a certificate's type has never needed that, because it is stored as a string on the Certificate row. Versioning the vocabulary would append a policy version every time DF add a word. So it is a TABLE OF ITS OWN, edited in place and audited on every change (ADR-019, last story). REMOVING A TYPE IS ALLOWED and rewrites nothing: the stored string is a snapshot in the sense grownUpsAtIssue is, and a record saved with a type DF later removed keeps showing it. That also makes the CertificateType row itself deletable — nothing references it, so deleting it destroys no history — which is the second exception to the project's no-deletes rule and is why it needs an ADR. SCHEMA CHANGE: yes, one new table with NO RELATIONS, so prisma/migrations/ is REGENERATED (pre-release) and THE HAND-WRITTEN PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX ON Customer.customerNumber MUST BE PUT BACK — story 2. NO use case, port or domain signature outside this feature changes: what reaches registerCustomer, renewCertificate and addToWaitingList is the same certificate with the same type string it took before. BUILD ORDER is inside-out: domain → schema/infrastructure → application → settings card → the shared control (with the counter as its first consumer) → the other four screens → e2e → docs. THE TWO THINGS MOST LIKELY TO GO WRONG: the re-added partial unique index (story 2), and PREFILL SILENTLY SUBSTITUTING — a form pre-filled from an archived record or a waiting-list entry whose type is not configured must land on „Sonstiges" with the old wording intact, never on a different type and never blank (stories 5 and 7).

userStories.title: The list of Nachweis-Arten is a validated domain value (domain)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the list of Nachweis-Arten to be a value with rules of its own, so that no screen and no adapter has to decide what counts as a duplicate. Source: tasks/prd-us-33-certificate-types-from-settings.md §US-33.1
acceptanceCriteria: NEW module src/domain/policy/certificateTypes.ts, beside eggs.ts. Its opening comment says it is the second list-valued thing DF configure and the FIRST THAT IS NOT A POLICY VALUE, and CITES ADR-019 rather than re-arguing it (the ADR itself is written in the last story of this batch — cite it anyway, it is the same PR)

CertificateTypeList = ReadonlyArray<string>, made ONLY by createCertificateTypeList(labels). The type is the invariant: a reader may rely on the order and on there being no duplicate — exactly as EggRule works
createCertificateTypeList TRIMS each label and returns the trimmed spelling

A label blank after trimming throws MissingRequiredField naming certificateTypes.<index>.label, with the index AS IT WAS TYPED so the form can mark the row on screen — the rule and the wording createEggRule already follows
A label longer than CERTIFICATE_TYPE_MAX_LENGTH (80, exported) throws a NEW CertificateTypeTooLong(length, maxLength) — same shape as NotesTooLong in src/domain/errors.ts

Two labels that FOLD TO THE SAME STRING throw a NEW DuplicateCertificateType(label) carrying the SECOND spelling as typed. Folding is foldName from src/domain/customer/nameSearch.ts — REUSED, NOT REWRITTEN. One line of comment says why a name-folding helper is the right one here; it does NOT re-explain what foldName does

The returned list is SORTED BY THE FOLDED LABEL ascending. Sorting is part of constructing the value, not something a caller does — staff type rows in whatever order they think of and the drop-down must not reorder between two saves
An EMPTY LIST is legitimate and means only „Sonstiges" is offered. It is NEVER read as "not configured", exactly as an empty egg rule is not

diffCertificateTypes(previous, next) returns ReadonlyArray<CertificateTypeChange> where CertificateTypeChange is { kind: "added" | "removed"; label: string }, in the list's own order, matched BY FOLDED LABEL. Re-spelling „jobcenter" as „Jobcenter" is therefore NO CHANGE; re-spelling it as „JC" is a removal and an addition
DuplicateCertificateType and CertificateTypeTooLong are added to src/domain/errors.ts in the file's existing shape: a readonly code and the offending values as readonly fields

WRITTEN TEST-FIRST, red → green → refactor, one named test per RULE (named after the rule, not the function): trims the spelling it stores / refuses a label that is only spaces / reads „Jobcenter" and „jobcenter" as one type / reads „Wohngeld" and „wohngeld " as one type / sorts umlauts where a German reader expects them / accepts an empty list as no configured types / reports a re-spelling as no change
The domain imports NOTHING from Next.js, React or Prisma, does no I/O and reads no clock — npm run lint enforces it via fd/domain-boundary
Domain coverage stays at 100%

The argument is of the required kind and is NOT the household-members one: nothing references the row, so deleting it destroys no history — a certificate carries its type as TEXT, not as a foreign key
